subject: Purchase method checklist and billing onramp — Acme Robotics pilot
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Carter <olivia.carter@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Purchase method checklist and billing onramp — Acme Robotics pilot

Hi Olivia — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and the start-of-billing for the 6-week pilot.

Call highlights (short):
- Pilot scope: 3 internal apps + sandbox integration for two engineers; expected peak traffic ~80k tokens/day across apps.
- Success criteria: 1) 3 integrations validated end-to-end, 2) average response latency <350ms p50 under realistic load, 3) annotated quality checks on 150 prompt samples.
- Billing preference: Acme suggested PO-driven procurement but also asked about marketplace purchase as a faster alternative.

Proposed commercial path options (choose one and we’ll prepare the paperwork):
1) PO + invoice: Standard enterprise route — we issue a quote and invoice monthly. Requires vendor form + W9 (if applicable) and a PO number to start billing.
2) Corporate card / marketplace: Fastest to get started (hours) but may have monthly spend limits; good for a quick proof-of-concept.
3) Hybrid: Start on card/marketplace for the first 1–2 weeks, then move to PO once procurement clears.

What we need from Acme to finalize start date:
- Confirm preferred payment path (PO or card)
- If PO: estimated PO number or expected date for PO issuance and contact in AP who will process invoices
- If card: confirm spending cap for initial pilot month
- Approve attached quote and SLA (I've attached both)

Attachments: Redwood_Quote_Acme_20261130.pdf (quote), SLA_Redwood_v1.pdf (standard pilot SLA).

Next steps / timeline (if you confirm today):
- If card: we can enable access and start test traffic within 24 hours.
- If PO: allow 5–10 business days after PO submission for vendor setup — we can provision a dedicated pilot environment as soon as we have the PO number.

I’ll wait for a short note with the preferred path and AP contact. Happy to hop on a quick 15-min alignment call if helpful.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein

Thanks Markus — helpful recap. A few answers and clarifying questions from our side:

Answers:
- We prefer PO for enterprise procurement. Our AP team requires a vendor setup packet (W-9 + vendor form).
- Estimated PO timeline: we should be able to issue a PO within 7–12 business days, pending internal approvals.

Questions:
- Can we start any integration work before the PO is fully processed (i.e., while vendor setup is underway)? We want to avoid losing momentum.
- What are the hard thresholds that would flip us from pilot to paid? We need concrete metrics to present to our product council.

AP contact: accounts-payable@acmerobotics.com (cc'd below in a separate message).

If possible, a hybrid approach sounds sensible — begin sandbox integration this week on a temporary card and switch billing to PO once vendor setup completes. Are there any limitations to that flow?

Regards,
Olivia Carter
Head of Product, Acme Robotics
olivia.carter@acmerobotics.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Carter <olivia.carter@acmerobotics.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Purchase method checklist and billing onramp — Acme Robotics pilot

Hi Olivia — quick follow from Redwood finance and ops side.

Short answers: yes, hybrid is supported and common. Practical details below.

If you want to start immediately (recommended for momentum):
- We can create a demo/temporary project tied to a corporate card to enable integration and initial validation within 24–48 hours.
- We will tag usage and export detailed usage reports to make month-of-transition billing seamless.

For PO + vendor setup (what we will need from Acme AP):
- Completed vendor form (attached stub: vendor_form_redwood.docx)
- Company billing address, Tax ID / EIN, and PO number to tie invoices to
- Contact name and email for invoice routing

Vendor setup timeline (typical): 5–12 business days after receiving the completed vendor packet. We can provision most pilot resources earlier (sandbox keys) but dedicated pilot pools and reserved mapping to the PO happen after vendor setup.

Pilot-to-paid triggers (recommended and negotiable):
1) Usage threshold: average sustained usage >= 75k tokens/day over a 7‑day window OR 20k embeddings API units/day for 7 days.
2) Operational: evidence of 3 successful end-to-end integrations and no critical latency regressions (p50 <350ms, error rate <1%).
3) Business: signed purchase order or subscription commitment.

If you want, we can bake these metrics into the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and attach as an appendix to the quote/SLA.

Attachments: vendor_form_redwood.docx (vendor packet stub).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Revenue Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 14:21:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Purchase method checklist and billing onramp — Acme Robotics pilot

Olivia — thanks. To keep momentum I recommend the hybrid path. Proposed immediate plan:
- Today: Olivia confirms we can use a corporate card for sandbox work and Acme provides a single technical contact (name + email) who will be given access.
- By EOD Fri (4 Dec): Redwood will enable sandbox keys and invite engineers to the demo workspace.
- Week of Dec 7: Acme submits vendor packet and we begin vendor setup. PO expected within 7–12 business days after submission.
- Transition: Once PO is live we issue the first monthly invoice tied to that PO and retroactively apply usage for the pilot month to the PO (no double billing).

Concrete asks for Acme to confirm today:
1) Card ok to start (Y/N) and initial spending cap for first 2 weeks (suggest $5k).
2) Technical contact for access (name + email).
3) AP contact for vendor packet routing (email).

Pilot success metrics (we will track these in Redwood Console):
- Integration count: 3 integrations green
- Quality checks: 150 annotated prompts with >=85% pass rate on product-defined rubric
- Latency & reliability: p50 <350ms, error rate <1% during test window

If you approve, I’ll open a HubSpot MAP and a DocuSign acceptance for the quote.

Thanks — available for a 15-min sync if needed.

Best,
Markus

For the sandbox start: we confirm Acme can approve a single-card usage for short-term testing. Please mark invoices as "Pilot - TBD PO" so AP can reconcile once PO is issued.
